learn.hook: Half of half a laddoo — is that a quarter? Multiplying fractions answers questions like this!
points: Fraction × fraction: multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators: 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2.
You can cancel common factors before multiplying to keep numbers small.
Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 gives an answer smaller than the number you started with.
learn.reallife: Recipes, discounts and sharing sweets all use 'fraction of' — like 3/4 of a kg of jalebis.

quiz.q: What is 3 × 2/5?
quiz.explain: 3 × 2/5 = 2/5 + 2/5 + 2/5 = 6/5. Only the numerator is multiplied by 3.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies both the numerator and the denominator by 3

quiz.q: Riya has 24 laddoos. She gives 1/4 of them to her neighbour. How many does she give?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 24 by 4 instead of finding a quarter

quiz.q: What is 2/3 × 3/4?
quiz.mistake: Adds the numerators and denominators instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Arjun walks 3/4 km every day. How far does he walk in 6 days?
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 and 3/4 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Which is true about 1/2 × 1/3?
options: It is 1/6, which is smaller than both fractions
quiz.explain: 1/2 × 1/3 = 1/6. Taking a part of a part gives something smaller than both.
quiz.mistake: Adds the denominators instead of multiplying them

quiz.q: Meena has ₹60 and spends 2/5 of it on a storybook. How much does the book cost?
quiz.mistake: Finds only 1/5 of the money

quiz.q: A card is 3/4 m long and 2/3 m wide. What is its area?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two lengths instead of multiplying

quiz.q: What is 1/2 of 1/2 of 40?
quiz.mistake: Takes half only once

teach.ask: Gappu wants to find 2/3 × 3/4. How do you multiply two fractions?
teach.praise: Yippee! Tops times tops, bottoms times bottoms — Gappu got 1/2!
teach.nudge: What do we do with the numerators and with the denominators?

learn.hook: How can 3 ÷ 1/4 be 12 — bigger than 3? Dividing by a fraction is full of surprises!
points: Dividing asks 'how many of these fit in?': 3 ÷ 1/4 asks how many quarters fit in 3. Answer: 12.
The reciprocal of a fraction is the fraction turned upside down: the reciprocal of 3/5 is 5/3.
To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal: 3/4 ÷ 1/8 = 3/4 × 8/1 = 6.
Dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a bigger answer. The number 0 has no reciprocal.

example.q: How many 1/4 kg packets of peanuts can be filled from 3 kg?

learn.reallife: Cutting a long ribbon into equal 3/4 m pieces, or filling 1/2 L bottles from a big can, means dividing by a fraction.

games.title: Division truths
items: Dividing by 1/2 is the same as multiplying by 2.
Dividing a number by a fraction less than 1 always makes it smaller.
No number times 0 gives 1, so 0 has no reciprocal.

quiz.q: What is the reciprocal of 4/9?
quiz.explain: Turn the fraction upside down: 4/9 becomes 9/4. Check: 4/9 × 9/4 = 1.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the reciprocal is the same fraction

quiz.q: How many halves are there in 5?
quiz.explain: 5 ÷ 1/2 = 5 × 2 = 10. Each whole has 2 halves, and 5 wholes have 10.
quiz.mistake: Divides 5 by 2 instead of dividing by 1/2

quiz.q: Kabir has 3 kg of rice and fills packets of 1/4 kg each. How many packets does he fill?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 3 by 1/4 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Find 2/3 ÷ 4.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 4 instead of dividing

quiz.q: What is 3/4 ÷ 3/8?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the fractions without flipping the second one

quiz.q: A ribbon is 7 1/2 m long. It is cut into pieces of 3/4 m. How many pieces are there?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies instead of dividing

quiz.q: Aisha shares 2/5 of a cake equally between 2 friends. What part of the whole cake does each friend get?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 2 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Which gives the biggest answer?
quiz.mistake: Thinks division always makes a number smaller

teach.ask: Gappu must divide 3/4 by 1/8. What is the trick for dividing by a fraction?
teach.praise: Woohoo! 3/4 × 8 = 6. Gappu found six 1/8 pieces in 3/4!
teach.nudge: After you flip the second fraction, what do you do?

learn.hook: Cooking for more guests, sharing pocket money, cutting ribbons — fractions are hiding in all of them!
points: 'Of' or 'part of' usually means multiply: 2/3 of 30 = 20.
'How many … fit in' or 'share equally' usually means divide.
Change mixed numbers like 2 1/2 into improper fractions (5/2) before multiplying or dividing.
Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 makes things smaller; dividing by it makes things bigger.
After solving, check that your answer makes sense for the story.

example.q: A recipe for 4 people needs 3/4 cup of sugar. How much sugar is needed for 6 people?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers sell 1/4 kg and 1/2 kg packets, and families scale recipes up for Diwali guests — all fraction maths!

games.title: Multiply or divide?
items: How many 1/2 L bottles can be filled from 6 L?
Cost of 3/4 kg at ₹80 per kg
Share 3/4 of a pizza equally among 3 friends
Area of a card 1/2 m by 1/3 m
How many 1/4-hour slots are in 2 hours?

quiz.q: A recipe for 4 people needs 3/4 cup of sugar. How much sugar is needed for 6 people?
quiz.explain: For 1 person: 3/4 ÷ 4 = 3/16 cup. For 6 people: 3/16 × 6 = 18/16 = 1 1/8 cups.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 3/4 by 6 without first finding the amount for one person

quiz.q: A train goes 60 km in one hour. How far does it go in 2 1/2 hours at the same speed?
quiz.mistake: Ignores the half hour or divides instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Aisha reads 2/5 of a 150-page book on Sunday. How many pages are left to read?
quiz.mistake: Gives the pages she read instead of the pages left

quiz.q: Harpreet pours a 2 L jug of lassi into glasses that hold 1/5 L each. How many glasses does she fill?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 2 by 1/5 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Joseph has a 5 m rope. He uses 1/2 of it, and then 1/3 of what is left. How much rope remains?
quiz.explain: After using half, 5/2 m is left. 1/3 of 5/2 is 5/6. Remaining: 5/2 − 5/6 = 15/6 − 5/6 = 10/6 = 1 2/3 m.
quiz.mistake: Takes 1/3 of the whole rope instead of 1/3 of what is left

quiz.q: A family eats 3/4 kg of rice every day. How much rice do they eat in a week?
quiz.mistake: Adds 7 and 3/4 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: ₹240 is shared. Riya gets 1/3 of it and Joseph gets 1/4 of it. How much money is left?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts only one person's share

quiz.q: Kabir multiplied 12 by 2/3 and got 18. Is his answer reasonable?
options: Yes — multiplying always makes a number bigger
No — multiplying by a fraction less than 1 should give less than 12
quiz.explain: 2/3 is less than 1, so 2/3 of 12 must be less than 12. The correct answer is 8.
quiz.mistake: Thinks multiplying always increases a number

teach.ask: Gappu is solving fraction stories. How does he know when to multiply and when to divide?
teach.praise: Brilliant! 'Of' means multiply, 'how many fit' means divide. Gappu is a fraction detective!
teach.nudge: Which word in a story tells you to multiply?
